business.text: She is building an ordering website for her friend's small bakery so customers can order bread ahead. It's a help-a-friend project; the bakery owner is someone else.

positioning.text: The bakery's edge is fresh, local bread, with a site that makes regulars feel the baker already knows them and secures their loaf, especially sourdough, before it sells out. Against walk-in queues and phone orders, it wins by being effortless and personal for people who already come in.

customers.text: First, the morning regulars who come in every day and hate finding the sourdough gone by nine. Occasional buyers, commuters and families come later.

whatSells.text: Good fresh bread, sourdough above all, the certainty it will be waiting, and the feeling of being recognised. In her words, don't ask for what you already know, so reserving the usual loaf should be near-zero effort: remembered details, one tap, repeatable.

brandFeel.text: Personal and familiar, like the baker already knows you. Warm, simple, local, with no needless questions.

strengths.text: She loves the customer journey, understanding customers' problems and building products that solve them, and she already knows her regulars' pain point. Questions for her should be about what customers struggle with and how ordering should flow, not technical or visual detail.

waysOfWorking.text: Probably hands-on and customer-led, thinking in terms of principles and how it feels to the customer, and wanting to know why a choice helps them. The team should settle technical and visual details itself and bring only customer and journey questions. Still largely an assumption.

philosophy.believe: I believe we build first for the morning regulars, the people who come every day and hate it when the sourdough is gone by nine.
philosophy.guidance: Design the first version around a regular reserving their usual loaf, sourdough above all, ahead of time so it's waiting for them. Keep browsing, picking, pickup day and confirming as quick as possible for repeat customers, and leave anything for first-time visitors until we have evidence.

philosophy.believe: Ordering should feel like being known: never ask for anything you could remember or skip.
philosophy.guidance: Remember each regular's usual loaf, pickup day and details, and prefill or skip them so reserving takes as few taps as possible. Use a warm, familiar tone, and only ask for what we truly don't know yet.
